answer.evidence: The object is a tall, narrow vertical wooden rib, 6 px wide, with gold bands at rows 17-18 and 30-31 and a grey metal foot at rows 43-47. It is drawn as a flat face-on strip with a dark outline at the sides. No band ends in a front-edge line with eave shadow, no ellipse is present, and no roof plane is present. The silhouette widens at the bands and at the foot, but these are wraps and a bracket, not horizontal surfaces. As a wall-mounted piece, it is a flat elevation with no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tall wooden rib with gold bands against a brick-and-stone wall, and it reads as a prop. It has 13 visible tones per full tile, which is above the hedge (9) and below the roofed well (20) and cheese stall (17). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. The wood and masonry show grain and per-stone variation, with about 4 steps per material against the references' 5-6. Outline pixels are 40% neutral, comparable to the well (33%) and bench (44%), and the rest lean brown. I read this as mixed, not a uniform black sticker line. It is slightly simpler than the best references but is at or above the mid-tier references (hedge, bench) on the primary facts, so a careful artist would accept it next to them.

It shows about 13 visible tones per 16x16 tile, which sits between prop-hedge (9) and prop-stall-cheese (17) and below prop-well-roofed (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills; the brick pattern, wood grain and bands break up every area. The wood and stone each have about 4-5 lightness steps, slightly short of Beodeul's 5-6 but not shallow. 40% of dark edge pixels are neutral, which is close to prop-bench-wood (44%) and prop-well-roofed (33%). That means the outline is partly tinted and partly dark neutral, so I call it mixed rather than a uniform black sticker line. Next to the references it does not look thinner or flatter, so it is acceptable, though not the richest piece.
